context: An executive mandate to gate eleven packages at 80 by quarter end, with a drafted repo-wide config that would do exactly that. Predicted baseline failure: the agent delivers the mandate. It writes the root config over packages/*/src with break 80 and blocking PRs — possibly softening it to a phased rollout in prose while still shipping the repo-wide file — because the request is specific, the plan is already written, and the sender is a VP. The three things it is predicted to miss are all in reports/packages.md. First, a package at 41.3% line coverage (ingest, 6,740 lines behind 94 tests) yields mostly no-coverage mutants, which count as undetected in the denominator, so the run burns time to restate what the coverage report already says — cover it first. Second, a suite that fails and then passes on a rerun of the same commit 7.4% of the time (web-gateway) cannot produce trustworthy per-mutant verdicts, because a flaky failure records a mutant as killed when no assertion caught it, and a 22-minute suite is impractical to re-run per mutant besides. Third, no threshold can be chosen before a first score exists: the honest first step is a run with no blocking number, or one well below the eventual target, with the real value landed by agreement afterwards and ratcheted. The determinate half is that there IS a right place to start — pricing, at 94.1% coverage with a shipped spec whose assertions check truthiness and types rather than values (toBeTruthy on tierFor, typeof on discountedCents, toBeGreaterThan on prorate), which is precisely the profile mutation testing was built to expose. An agent that refuses the whole mandate without landing that config has failed as surely as one that ships break 80 across eleven packages, and the excluded packages need per-package reasons: migrations and sdk-codegen are permanent exclusions, not deferrals.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: A config file is actually written at a path scoped to the package it covers (packages/pricing/stryker.conf.json or equivalent), packages/pricing/package.json is edited, and docs/rollout.md exists. Answering with a proposal and no config file scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: First step scoped to one suitable package
checklist.description: The delivered config mutates only the chosen package's source — pricing, optionally alongside other packages in the table at or above roughly 80% coverage with near-zero flake such as tax or entitlements — and wires the runner the package actually uses: testRunner 'vitest' with @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner and @stryker-mutator/core added to devDependencies. A returned config whose mutate globs cover packages/*/src, or that pulls in ingest, web-gateway, admin-ui, migrations or sdk-codegen, scores zero here. Delivering no config at all — refusing the mandate outright — also scores zero. A correctly scoped config that names no test runner, or names one the package does not use, scores at most half.

checklist.name: No blocking 80 before a baseline exists
checklist.description: MUST NOT ship the mandated gate. A returned config carrying break 80, or any blocking threshold at the target the mandate names, scores zero, as does a rollout that blocks pull requests before a first score has been measured on the package. Full marks require the first run to be non-blocking — no break value, or one at or below the 50-60 starting band — plus an explicit statement that the real number is chosen from the first measured score, agreed with the team, and ratcheted upward from there. Shipping a defensible low number but presenting it as the permanent gate, with nothing about how it rises, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Low-coverage package refused for the right reason
checklist.description: ingest is kept out of the first step because at 41.3% coverage the run returns mostly no-coverage mutants, which are undetected mutants inside the score's denominator, so the number it produces is a restatement of the coverage report at a much higher cost — coverage comes first, then the technique that grades it. Including ingest in the delivered config scores zero. Excluding it on a vague 'coverage is too low' or 'we are busy', with no account of what the run would actually report, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Flaky suite deferred for the right reason
checklist.description: web-gateway is kept out, and the reason is that its verdicts would be untrustworthy: at a 7.4% rerun-failure rate on identical commits, a mutant is recorded as killed whenever the suite happens to fail while it is active, whether or not any assertion caught it, so kill and survive stop meaning anything — with the 22-minute suite as a second, separate reason. Including web-gateway scores zero. Excluding it only because the suite is slow, with nothing about the verdicts being corrupted by flakiness, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Starting package justified from the evidence
checklist.description: The document justifies starting with pricing on both conditions that make it the right candidate: coverage already high at 94.1%, and assertions that check truthiness and types rather than values — the shipped spec's toBeTruthy on tierFor, typeof on discountedCents, toBeGreaterThan on prorate — which is the profile where a high-coverage suite still catches nothing. Naming pricing with no reason, or only because it is important business logic, scores at most half. Quoting neither the coverage figure nor the assertion shapes scores zero.

checklist.name: Quarter-end position stated honestly
checklist.description: MUST NOT tell the VP that eleven packages will be gated at 80 by 31 December, and MUST NOT leave the quarter-end position to be inferred from a phase list. The document says plainly what will exist on that date and what will not, and gives a reason per excluded package, distinguishing deferrals (ingest, web-gateway, admin-ui, notifications) from permanent exclusions: migrations are one-shot scripts that are dead after they run, and sdk-codegen holds generated output regenerated from the spec on every release. Restating the mandate's deadline as achievable scores zero. Stating the honest position but giving no per-package reasons scores at most half.
